subject: Skyline AI - throughput degradation, error spike and remediation / credit discussion
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@skylineai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@skylineai.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Severe throughput degradation — immediate remediation & credit request

Jonas —

We saw a sustained throughput drop and elevated 5xx/error rates between 02:00–06:30 UTC this morning that materially impacted our inference pipelines. Latency for our 512-token baseline jumped from ~180ms to ~850ms and handled throughput dropped by ~60%. This caused timeouts in batch jobs and an incomplete run for three customer demos.

We reported via support ticket #93011 at 05:01 UTC; we've attached a short log excerpt and timeline. Given the business impact, Skyline needs:
- A clear incident timeline and root cause summary within 24 hours
- A proposed remediation and prevention plan
- A commercial remediation: we expect compensation for degraded SLA days and expedited review with execs if necessary

Please confirm receipt and senior ownership.

Attachments: Skyline_error_snapshot.log (excerpt)

—Marco
Head of Platform
Skyline AI
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@skylineai.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput degradation — immediate remediation & credit request

Marco — thanks for the heads up and the log. I’m really sorry Skyline was hit this morning. I’ve looped in Hannah (CS lead), Ben (your account rep), and Laura (legal) so we can coordinate. High-level next steps from my side:
1) We’ll triage the support ticket immediately and provide a first-pass incident timeline within 6 hours.
2) Hannah will share the infra/metric snapshot and a provisional mitigation plan.
3) Ben and I will prepare a commercial remediation outline for review and — if needed — an exec sync.

We understand the demos were impacted; that elevates this to exec priority. I’ve scheduled an optional internal war room and we’ll follow up with a proposed time for a cross-company call.

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@skylineai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput degradation — immediate remediation & credit request

Marco / team — quick diagnostic summary below (high level):
- Window impacted: 2026-12-12T02:05:00Z — 2026-12-12T06:28:00Z
- Root cause (prelim): autoscaler regression interacting with a recent runtime kernel change; resulted in unusually long cold-starts and queue buildup for multi-tenant pools servicing Skyline traffic.
- Observed metrics: 5xx rate peaked at 7.9% (baseline 0.3%), p95 latency ~860ms (baseline ~180ms), ingress dropped ~58% vs baseline throughput.

Immediate mitigations applied by 11:45 UTC: forced rollback of the kernel change, manual pool rebalancing, and temporary traffic isolation for Skyline to a reserved pool. Early signs show steady improvement to baseline by 07:00 UTC.

Proposed remediation options for commercial team to consider (I also attached a spreadsheet with calculations):
A) One-time credit equal to proportionate monthly invoice reduction for impacted hours (calculated in attached sheet).
B) Fixed-month credit (e.g., 10% of monthly committed spend) for the impacted billing period plus a service-level addendum to guarantee isolation windows for dedicated pools during major rollouts.

I’ll finalize a full postmortem with timeline and RCA by Monday EOD. Attaching: sla_calculation_sheet.xlsx (workbook with hour-by-hour impact and example credit calculations).

—Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@skylineai.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput degradation — immediate remediation & credit request

Marco — thanks for the patience. From a commercial perspective I want to keep this pragmatic and fast:
Option 1 (provisional, no amendment): a one-time credit equivalent to the calculated impacted token-hours (see Hannah's sheet) applied to your next invoice.
Option 2 (contractual): a one-time credit plus a short contract amendment we can sign that commits Redwood to accelerated rollback and a guaranteed isolation plan for any future kernel changes affecting your dedicated pools — this would also include a $Xk makewhole commitment if SLA triggers are exceeded in the future quarter.

If Skyline prefers option 2, Laura can draft a short amendment and I can route it for approval. If speed is priority, we can provision Option 1 immediately and follow with a formal amendment. What would you prefer for the exec/decision call?

—Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@skylineai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick diagnostics and the rollback. We are okay moving forward with Option 2 — we need contractual assurance because this impacted two external demos and several late-stage customers.

Requests before the amendment is finalized:
- A clear timeline for delivery of the postmortem and the mitigation checklist (Hannah to Monday EOD)
- Draft amendment to include: defined isolation windows, rollback SLOs, and a defined credit formula that references consumed token-hours during incident windows
- DocuSign or equivalent so we can route internally on our side quickly

We can do an exec sync/30m on Tuesday 2026-12-15 at 10:00 PST if that works for Redwood. Marco
